sets.title: Why Coral Reefs Matter
sets.titleEs: Por qué importan los arrecifes de coral

learn.rule: A paragraph has one big idea, the topic sentence. Every detail sentence must support it, and details that do not belong get cut.
learn.ruleEs: Un párrafo tiene una idea principal, la oración temática. Cada oración de detalle debe apoyarla, y los detalles que no pertenecen se eliminan.
learn.model: Coral reefs are valuable to both ocean life and people. Thousands of fish species shelter and feed among the coral.
learn.notice: The first sentence names the big idea. The second sentence is one detail that supports it.

items.prompt: Choose the topic sentence that covers all three reef details.
items.text: Details: Reefs shelter thousands of fish species. Reef walls slow ocean waves before they reach land. Divers and fishers earn a living from healthy reefs.

options.text: Coral is a kind of animal that builds hard skeletons from limestone.
Coral reefs are valuable for nature and for people.
I am going to write about reefs.
Some of the largest reefs on Earth are found near Australia.

items.why: A topic sentence has to be big enough to cover every detail. The other choices are too narrow or only announce a subject.
items.whyEs: Una oración temática debe ser lo bastante amplia para cubrir todos los detalles. Las otras opciones son muy estrechas o solo anuncian un tema.

items.prompt: Check the details that belong in a paragraph about why reefs matter.

options.text: Reefs give fish and crabs places to hide from predators.
My cousin likes to collect shells at the beach.
Tourism around reefs brings visitors who spend money in nearby towns.
The new science museum opens on Saturday.
Reefs slow waves, which helps protect shorelines from erosion.

items.why: A detail belongs only when it supports the topic sentence. The two details about shells and the museum are about something else.
items.whyEs: Un detalle pertenece solo si apoya la oración temática. Los detalles sobre las conchas y el museo tratan de otra cosa.

items.prompt: Put the sentences in order to build the paragraph about coral reefs.
lines: Coral reefs matter to both ocean life and people.
First, they give thousands of species a place to feed and hide.
Second, they slow waves, which protects shorelines from erosion.
Finally, they provide jobs in fishing and tourism for coastal communities.
For these reasons, protecting reefs benefits everyone.
items.why: The topic sentence comes first, the details follow in order with signal words, and the closing sentence comes last.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero, los detalles siguen en orden con palabras de señal y la oración final va al último.

items.prompt: Complete the reef topic sentence so the details support it.
parts: habitats because they support ocean life and human communities.
items.model: Coral reefs are valuable habitats because they support ocean life and human communities.
items.why: Valuable is a claim that the details can support. Warm and far do not connect to the reasons in the sentence.
items.whyEs: Valuable es una idea que los detalles pueden apoyar. Warm y far no se conectan con las razones de la oración.

items.prompt: Which closing sentence best finishes the coral reef paragraph?
items.text: Coral reefs matter to both ocean life and people. They shelter thousands of species. They also slow waves and protect shorelines. Finally, they create jobs in fishing and tourism.

options.text: In conclusion, healthy reefs are worth protecting because nature and coastal communities both depend on them.
Reefs are colorful, and many divers enjoy seeing their bright fish.
Another important ocean habitat is the kelp forest, which grows in cool water.
Many people have never seen a reef, but pictures help them imagine one.

items.why: A strong closing sentence wraps up the big idea. It does not add a new topic or repeat one small fact.
items.whyEs: Una buena oración final cierra la idea principal. No agrega un tema nuevo ni repite un solo dato pequeño.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two detail sentences about mangrove forests. Use the notes.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos oraciones de detalle sobre los manglares. Usa las notas.
write.text: Topic: Why mangrove forests matter. Notes: roots slow floodwater; young fish hide in the roots; trees store carbon.
write.frame: Mangrove forests matter because ___. First, ___. Also, ___.

label: I wrote at least 25 words
Escribí al menos 25 palabras
I used signal words such as first, also, or finally
Usé palabras de señal como first, also o finally
I used a detail from the notes
Usé un detalle de las notas
My last sentence ends with a period
Mi última oración termina con punto

write.model: Mangrove forests protect coasts and the creatures that live near them. First, their thick roots slow floodwater and keep soil in place. Also, young fish hide in the roots until they are strong enough to survive in open water.

familyTalk.en: At dinner, name a place you love and give one big idea about it. Then each person adds a detail that supports it.
familyTalk.es: En la cena, nombren un lugar que les guste y den una idea principal sobre él. Luego cada persona agrega un detalle que la apoye.

teacherTip.en: Have pairs test each detail with the question: does this support the topic sentence? Cut any that do not.
teacherTip.es: Pide a las parejas que prueben cada detalle con la pregunta: ¿esto apoya la oración temática? Que eliminen los que no.

sets.title: The Silk Road Paragraph
sets.titleEs: El párrafo de la Ruta de la Seda

learn.rule: A paragraph has one big idea, the topic sentence. Every detail sentence must support it, and details that do not belong get cut.
learn.ruleEs: Un párrafo tiene una idea principal, la oración temática. Cada oración de detalle debe apoyarla, y los detalles que no pertenecen se eliminan.
learn.model: The Silk Road linked distant parts of the world through trade and shared ideas. Merchants carried silk from China, and travelers carried ideas such as papermaking toward the west.
learn.notice: The first sentence is the big idea. The second sentence gives examples of goods and ideas that moved.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence covers all three details about the Silk Road?
items.text: Camel caravans carried silk, spices, and glass across deserts. Oasis towns grew rich by selling food and water to travelers. Buddhism and papermaking spread along the same routes.

options.text: Camels can travel long distances without much water or food.
Silk was first made in China thousands of years ago.
This paragraph is about the Silk Road.
The Silk Road was a network of routes that moved goods, wealth, and ideas.

items.why: The best topic sentence covers goods, wealth, and ideas, which are all three details. The others are single facts or an announcement.
items.whyEs: La mejor oración temática cubre los bienes, la riqueza y las ideas, que son los tres detalles. Las otras son datos sueltos o un anuncio.

items.prompt: Check the sentences that support a paragraph about the Silk Road.

options.text: Traders exchanged spices, glass, and silk in busy market towns.
Many travelers joined caravans for safety on long journeys.
A high-speed train now connects Beijing and Shanghai.
Papermaking knowledge traveled westward along the trade routes.
Many students enjoy reading about ancient history.

items.why: Supporting details stay on the topic of the Silk Road. A modern train and an opinion about students are off topic.
items.whyEs: Los detalles de apoyo se quedan en el tema de la Ruta de la Seda. Un tren moderno y una opinión sobre estudiantes se salen del tema.

items.prompt: Which sentence is off topic in this Silk Road paragraph?
items.text: The Silk Road connected China with the Mediterranean world. Merchants moved silk, spices, and paper along its routes. Camel caravans crossed deserts and mountain passes. Our school cafeteria serves lunch at noon. Oasis towns grew rich by serving travelers. Ideas and religions also traveled the road.

options.text: Our school cafeteria serves lunch at noon.
Camel caravans crossed deserts and mountain passes.
Oasis towns grew rich by serving travelers.
Ideas and religions also traveled the road.

items.why: Read each sentence and ask whether it supports the topic. The cafeteria sentence says nothing about the Silk Road, so it should be cut.
items.whyEs: Lee cada oración y pregunta si apoya el tema. La oración de la cafetería no dice nada sobre la Ruta de la Seda, así que se debe eliminar.

items.prompt: Put the Silk Road sentences in order to make a clear paragraph.
lines: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes that connected China with lands near the Mediterranean Sea.
First, caravans carried silk, spices, and glass between distant markets.
Second, oasis towns along the way grew wealthy by selling food and water to travelers.
Finally, religions and inventions, such as Buddhism and papermaking, spread along the same routes.
In short, the Silk Road connected people through goods, wealth, and ideas.
items.why: Start with the big idea, use first, second, and finally to order the details, and end with a closing sentence.
items.whyEs: Empieza con la idea principal, usa first, second y finally para ordenar los detalles, y termina con una oración final.

items.prompt: Finish the closing sentence about the Silk Road.
parts: In conclusion, the Silk Road was important because it
distant cultures and allowed goods and ideas to
items.model: In conclusion, the Silk Road was important because it connected distant cultures and allowed goods and ideas to spread.
items.why: A closing sentence restates the big idea. The Silk Road connected cultures and let goods and ideas spread, so those words fit.
items.whyEs: Una oración final repite la idea principal. La Ruta de la Seda conectó culturas y permitió que bienes e ideas se difundieran, así que esas palabras encajan.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two detail sentences about Roman roads. Use the notes.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos oraciones de detalle sobre los caminos romanos. Usa las notas.
write.text: Topic: Why Roman roads helped the empire. Notes: soldiers marched quickly; merchants moved goods; messengers carried news.
write.frame: Roman roads helped the empire because ___. First, ___. Also, ___.

label: I wrote at least 25 words
Escribí al menos 25 palabras
I used signal words such as first, also, or finally
Usé palabras de señal como first, also o finally
I used a detail from the notes
Usé un detalle de las notas
My last sentence ends with a period
Mi última oración termina con punto

write.model: Roman roads helped hold a huge empire together. First, soldiers could march quickly to places that needed protection. Also, merchants and messengers used the same roads to move goods and news from city to city.

familyTalk.en: Ask someone at home how people in their family traveled or sent news long ago. Share one big idea and two details.
familyTalk.es: Pregunten a alguien en casa cómo viajaban o enviaban noticias en su familia hace tiempo. Compartan una idea principal y dos detalles.

teacherTip.en: Display the cafeteria sentence and ask students to explain in one sentence why it is off topic.
teacherTip.es: Muestra la oración de la cafetería y pide que expliquen en una oración por qué se sale del tema.

learn.rule: In a literary paragraph, the topic sentence makes a claim about the story, and each detail gives evidence from the text.
learn.ruleEs: En un párrafo literario, la oración temática hace una afirmación sobre el cuento y cada detalle da evidencia del texto.
learn.model: In 'The Last Ferry,' the foggy harbor makes the mood tense and lonely. The empty docks and the muffled bell show that no one else is nearby.
learn.notice: The topic sentence is a claim about mood. The detail sentence points to evidence in the setting.

items.prompt: Choose the topic sentence that the story details support.
items.text: Details from 'The Last Ferry': The fog is so thick that Mara cannot see the water. The only sound is a bell ringing far away. The benches on the dock are empty, and the ticket window is dark.

options.text: Mara is waiting at the dock for the last ferry to arrive.
Fog is made of tiny drops of water.
The setting of 'The Last Ferry' creates a lonely, uneasy mood.
I think the story is interesting and I would like to read more.

items.why: All three details show a lonely, uneasy place, so the topic sentence names that mood. The other choices are too narrow, off topic, or only an opinion.
items.whyEs: Los tres detalles muestran un lugar solitario e inquietante, así que la oración temática nombra ese ambiente. Las otras opciones son muy estrechas, se salen del tema o solo dan una opinión.

items.prompt: Check the details that support the lonely mood in 'The Last Ferry.'

options.text: The dock lights flicker, and no other passengers appear.
Mara's backpack is green and has two zippers.
Mara hears her own footsteps echo on the wet boards.
The author has written several other stories.
The ticket window is dark, and the schedule board is blank.

items.why: Evidence for a mood describes what the character sees and hears in the setting. The backpack color and the author's other books do not build the mood.
items.whyEs: La evidencia del ambiente describe lo que el personaje ve y oye en el escenario. El color de la mochila y los otros libros del autor no crean el ambiente.

items.prompt: Put the sentences in order to build the paragraph about 'The Last Ferry.'
lines: The setting of 'The Last Ferry' makes the mood tense and lonely.
First, thick fog hides the water, so Mara feels cut off from the world.
Next, the dark ticket window and empty benches show that no one else is coming.
Finally, the distant bell is the only sound, which makes the silence feel even heavier.
Together, these details make readers share Mara's uneasy waiting.
items.why: The claim comes first, the evidence follows in order, and the last sentence ties the details back to the claim.
items.whyEs: La afirmación va primero, la evidencia sigue en orden y la última oración une los detalles con la afirmación.

items.prompt: Choose the words that connect the evidence to the claim.
parts: Mara cannot see the water. This detail
the topic sentence about a lonely mood.
items.model: The fog is thick, so Mara cannot see the water. This detail supports the topic sentence about a lonely mood.
items.why: So shows a result: thick fog leads to Mara not seeing the water. Supports tells readers that the detail proves the claim.
items.whyEs: So muestra un resultado: la niebla espesa hace que Mara no vea el agua. Supports dice al lector que el detalle prueba la afirmación.

items.prompt: Which sentence best closes the paragraph about 'The Last Ferry'?
items.text: The setting of 'The Last Ferry' makes the mood tense and lonely. Thick fog hides the water and cuts Mara off from the world. The dark ticket window and empty benches show that no one else is coming. The only sound is a distant bell.

options.text: Mara waits at the dock for the last ferry of the night.
Overall, the author uses fog, darkness, and silence to make readers feel Mara's loneliness.
Ferries are boats that carry passengers across the water.
The next story in the book is about a mountain village.

items.why: A closing sentence pulls the evidence together and returns to the claim. It does not retell one detail or start a new topic.
items.whyEs: Una oración final reúne la evidencia y vuelve a la afirmación. No repite un solo detalle ni empieza un tema nuevo.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two detail sentences about how a stormy night setting can build suspense.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos oraciones de detalle sobre cómo un escenario de noche con tormenta puede crear suspenso.
write.text: Topic: How a stormy night setting can create suspense in a story. Notes: thunder shakes the windows; the power goes out; a door creaks upstairs.
write.frame: A stormy night setting can build suspense because ___. First, ___. Then, ___.

label: I wrote at least 25 words
Escribí al menos 25 palabras
I used signal words such as first, also, or finally
Usé palabras de señal como first, also o finally
I used a detail from the notes
Usé un detalle de las notas
My last sentence ends with a period
Mi última oración termina con punto

write.model: A stormy night setting can build suspense in a story. First, thunder shakes the windows, which makes the characters jump at every sound. Then the power goes out, and a creaking door upstairs makes the darkness feel dangerous.

familyTalk.en: Describe a place from a book or movie you both know. Say one claim about its mood and two details that prove it.
familyTalk.es: Describan un lugar de un libro o una película que ambos conozcan. Digan una afirmación sobre su ambiente y dos detalles que la prueben.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to underline the words in each detail that create the mood, then connect them to the claim.
teacherTip.es: Pide que subrayen las palabras de cada detalle que crean el ambiente y que las conecten con la afirmación.
